INVESTIGATION REPORT

Claim Reference: Confidential
Date of Loss: [Redacted]

FINDINGS
Investigation of the loss site revealed significant heat damage originating at the electrical distribution panel in the utility room. Arc marks consistent with an electrical fault were observed on two breakers. The adjacent wiring showed heat deformation extending outward from the panel.

PROBABLE CAUSE
Based on physical evidence, the fire originated from an electrical fault at the main distribution panel. Arc damage and heat patterns are consistent with a short circuit or overloaded circuit condition.

CONCLUSION
The cause of the fire is confirmed as an electrical fault at the distribution panel. No evidence of accelerants or other ignition sources was identified.

INVESTIGATION REPORT

Claim Reference: Confidential

FINDINGS
The vehicle sustained fire damage beginning at the engine compartment. Witnesses reported seeing smoke from under the hood approximately 10 minutes before the fire became visible. The fuel system showed no leaks. An oil-soaked rag was found near the air filter housing.

PROBABLE CAUSE
The most probable cause of the fire is an unattended ignition source in the engine compartment, possibly the oil-soaked material near a heat source. However, this cannot be confirmed due to the extent of fire damage to the engine components.

CONCLUSION
Cause is probable but not confirmed. Further analysis of engine components was not possible due to fire damage.

INVESTIGATION REPORT

Claim Reference: Confidential

FINDINGS
Water intrusion was identified across the second floor of the structure. Moisture mapping indicated the point of entry to be the roof assembly above the master bedroom. Roof membrane showed cracking consistent with age-related deterioration. No storm event occurred in the 72 hours preceding discovery.

PROBABLE CAUSE
Roof membrane failure due to age and deferred maintenance.

CONCLUSION
The cause of water damage is confirmed as roof membrane failure. No weather event contributed to this loss.

INVESTIGATION REPORT

Claim Reference: Confidential

FINDINGS
Vehicle was recovered from a ditch off a rural highway. Front-end damage consistent with collision. Airbags deployed. No other vehicle was involved. Tire tread depth was within acceptable limits. Road surface was dry.

PROBABLE CAUSE
Driver error is the probable cause. However, no witness statements were obtained and driver declined to provide a statement.

CONCLUSION
Cause is probable. Driver error (loss of vehicle control) is the most likely explanation but cannot be confirmed without additional evidence.

INVESTIGATION REPORT

Claim Reference: Confidential

FINDINGS
Claimant reported discovering mold growth behind drywall in the basement after conducting minor renovations. A moisture survey identified an active slow leak from the water heater supply line. The leak appeared to have been present for several months based on staining patterns and mold growth extent.

PROBABLE CAUSE
Slow leak from the water heater supply line connection.

CONCLUSION
The cause of mold damage is confirmed as a long-term water intrusion from a defective water heater supply line fitting.

INVESTIGATION REPORT

Claim Reference: Confidential

FINDINGS
Extensive review of the scene was conducted following a reported slip and fall at the insured commercial premises. The floor surface at the incident location showed no visible moisture or contaminant at the time of inspection (conducted 48 hours after the incident). No CCTV footage was available. A single witness reported seeing a wet spot in the area earlier that day but could not confirm it was present at the time of the incident.

PROBABLE CAUSE
Cannot be determined with available evidence.

CONCLUSION
Cause of the slip and fall cannot be determined. The presence or absence of a hazardous floor condition at the time of the incident is not supported by sufficient evidence.

INVESTIGATION REPORT

Claim Reference: Confidential

FINDINGS
Kitchen fire with point of origin at the stovetop. Pots and pans were found on active burners. Neighbour confirmed the claimant had left the property approximately two hours before the fire was discovered. No evidence of accelerants.

PROBABLE CAUSE
Unattended cooking.

CONCLUSION
The cause of the fire is confirmed as an unattended cooking appliance. The claimant left the property while burners were active.

INVESTIGATION REPORT

Claim Reference: Confidential

FINDINGS
Review of medical records indicates the patient was prescribed medication A but received medication B during a three-day inpatient stay. The dispensing error was identified on day four when the patient reported symptoms inconsistent with the expected treatment response. Pharmacy records confirm the dispensing discrepancy.

PROBABLE CAUSE
Pharmacy dispensing error.

CONCLUSION
The cause of the adverse medical event is confirmed as a medication dispensing error. Records are consistent and the chain of custody for the dispensing error is documented.

INVESTIGATION REPORT

Claim Reference: Confidential

FINDINGS
Structural inspection following reported water damage identified deteriorating caulking around the exterior window frames on the south and west elevations. Moisture mapping confirmed water entry through the window surround. The building is 22 years old and maintenance records provided show no window caulking has been replaced in that period.

PROBABLE CAUSE
Deferred maintenance of window seals.

CONCLUSION
The probable cause of water intrusion is failure of aged window caulking. No acute weather event was required to initiate this loss; normal rainfall was sufficient given the deteriorated state of the seals.

INVESTIGATION REPORT

Claim Reference: Confidential

FINDINGS
Vehicle fire occurred in a parking lot. Point of origin was in the rear cargo area. No mechanical or electrical fault was identified in the engine or fuel systems. An accelerant odor was noted by the first attending fire crew, but the odour had dissipated by the time the investigator arrived 90 minutes later. No accelerant residue was detected in laboratory analysis of debris samples.

PROBABLE CAUSE
Unable to determine. Incendiary origin cannot be confirmed or excluded.

CONCLUSION
Cause is not determinable. Physical evidence is insufficient to establish whether the fire was accidental or incendiary.

INVESTIGATION REPORT

Claim Reference: Confidential

FINDINGS
Investigation of a commercial burglary revealed a forced entry through the rear service door. Door jamb damage is consistent with a pry tool. Alarm system logs show the alarm was triggered at 02:14 but the system provider records show notification was delayed 47 minutes due to a monitoring center backlog. Stolen items include computing equipment, a small safe, and power tools.

PROBABLE CAUSE
Opportunistic burglary facilitated by an unmonitored entry point and a delayed alarm response.

CONCLUSION
The cause of the loss is confirmed as a commercial burglary. Entry method and timeline are clearly established by physical evidence and system logs.

INVESTIGATION REPORT

Claim Reference: Confidential

FINDINGS
Claimant submitted a claim for a wristwatch reported stolen during a hotel stay. No evidence of forced entry to the room was found. Hotel keycard access logs show the room was accessed by the claimant and one hotel staff member (for housekeeping) during the reported window. The claimant could not confirm the watch was in the room at check-in.

PROBABLE CAUSE
Unknown. Theft by hotel staff is possible but not supported by evidence. The item may not have been brought to the hotel.

CONCLUSION
Cause of loss cannot be determined. Insufficient evidence to confirm theft occurred at this location.

INVESTIGATION REPORT

Claim Reference: Confidential

FINDINGS
Pipe burst in an exterior wall during a cold weather event. Temperatures dropped to -22C over a 48-hour period. The pipe in question was a domestic water supply line running through an uninsulated exterior wall cavity. Adjacent pipes in insulated cavities were unaffected.

PROBABLE CAUSE
Freezing of an uninsulated supply pipe during an extreme cold weather event.

CONCLUSION
The cause of the water damage is confirmed as a frozen and burst pipe. The lack of insulation in the wall cavity is the contributing factor that allowed freezing at the recorded temperatures.

INVESTIGATION REPORT

Claim Reference: Confidential

FINDINGS
Review of records following a reported product liability claim. A customer alleged that a blender purchased from the insured retailer caused injury when the blade assembly detached during use. Examination of the returned unit showed the blade locking mechanism had not been fully engaged at assembly. Manufacturing batch records were reviewed; two additional units from the same batch were inspected and found to have the same assembly defect.

PROBABLE CAUSE
Manufacturing defect in the blade locking assembly for this production batch.

CONCLUSION
The cause of the injury is confirmed as a product defect. The blade assembly failure is attributable to an error in the manufacturing process for this batch.

INVESTIGATION REPORT

Claim Reference: Confidential

FINDINGS
A vehicle was reported stolen from a residential driveway. The claimant reported the vehicle missing in the morning. Keyless entry fob was found inside the home. No signs of forced entry to the vehicle. Neighbourhood canvass produced no witnesses. Police report was filed.

PROBABLE CAUSE
Vehicle theft, method undetermined. Relay attack on the keyless entry system is possible given no physical evidence of forced entry, but cannot be confirmed.

CONCLUSION
Cause of loss is probable theft. Method of vehicle access cannot be determined from available evidence.

INVESTIGATION REPORT

Claim Reference: Confidential

FINDINGS
Fire damage to a detached garage. Point of origin identified at a workbench area. Multiple solvent containers (paint thinner, mineral spirits) were stored in open containers on the bench. A space heater was found in the area. Damage patterns are consistent with an accelerated fire due to the presence of volatile solvents.

PROBABLE CAUSE
Ignition of volatile solvent vapours from the space heater.

CONCLUSION
The probable cause of the fire is ignition of solvent vapours by the nearby space heater. This cannot be confirmed as the ignition point was not preserved in the debris.

INVESTIGATION REPORT

Claim Reference: Confidential

FINDINGS
Commercial property sustained hail damage during a storm event on [date redacted]. Hail size was reported at 3-4cm by Environment Canada data for the area. Roof membrane damage, skylight cracking, and denting of HVAC equipment were observed. Damage is consistent with the reported hail event.

PROBABLE CAUSE
Hail impact during the reported storm event.

CONCLUSION
The cause of the property damage is confirmed as hail impact. Damage patterns and meteorological data are consistent.

INVESTIGATION REPORT

Claim Reference: Confidential

FINDINGS
A claim was submitted for water damage to a finished basement. Investigation found no evidence of pipe failure, appliance leak, or roof/foundation infiltration. The sump pump was operational at time of inspection. The claimant reported the damage was discovered after an extended absence. Neighbours reported heavy rainfall during the period in question.

PROBABLE CAUSE
Sump pump overwhelm or failure during a high-rainfall event, with recovery before the inspection date. However, this cannot be confirmed as no failure evidence remains.

CONCLUSION
Cause cannot be determined with certainty. A transient sump pump failure during heavy rainfall is the most probable explanation but is not supported by physical evidence at time of inspection.
